question: Can a passive, opt-in, host-only event stream distinguish a native seat entering its agent and its actual play outcome while another seat still has no terminal evidence?
contrasts: An unmodified two-Oracle shipping config with observer off and on: same native seat dispositions, world reward of 1, six unscoped native event names and original default result schema; only the opt-in run creates the new journal.

Hello-seats uses scripted native participants. After honest stock Oracle work, the tested seat delays; the supporting seat can return, hold for a supervisor stop, self-cancel, or raise. In the deadline case both hold. A separate intentional setup refusal happens before either player runs.
pass: For all seven opted-in attempts, final ordering is gapless in one host process, no raw prompts or arbitrary diagnostic payloads appear, and every recorded terminal disposition equals the native seat result.
Every expected play entry has one observed entry. Both setup-refusal seats have no entry or terminal event. A snapshot of an open or partial journal never reports an unobserved return.
For support-return, at least one external host snapshot while result.json is absent reports the supporting seat ended and no terminal for the tested seat.
The disabled control produces no journal. Do not rewrite the failure into a pass if any registered case disagrees.
limits: A run_enter means the native runner is about to invoke agent.run. It is not a model request, message receipt, spend, tool execution, or evidence of attention.
The play_end event reports the play-scope finalizer, not container or child process termination. EOF without closed is not a crash diagnosis.
Any owner-side recovery experiments on partial lines or errors are separate from the registered native cohort. No retry can replace one of these 8 starts.
2 or fewer local wrapped Docker trials at a time. No model seats, no provider keys, $0.
